title: Prune directory traversal for ignored directories in inverted scans
body:
This PR fixes a bug where `skipInternal: true` failed to prune directory traversal during inverted scans (`invert: true` or `invert: 2`).

### The Bug
Previously, whether to skip a directory's traversal was tied to `isExcluded` (which depends on `invert`). During an inverted scan (returning only ignored files), non-ignored directories (e.g. `src/`) were incorrectly pruned (setting `result.next = 1`), while ignored directories (e.g. `node_modules/`) were recursively traversed (leaving `result.next = 0`), triggering thousands of redundant file reads and parser runs (such as reading `package.json` for every package inside `node_modules/`).

### The Fix
This PR separates directory traversal pruning from the final results exclusion check in `walkIncludes` (`src/walk.ts`). We now set `result.next = 1` immediately if `isDir && skipInternal && match.ignored`, regardless of the final inverted/not-inverted status.

Comprehensive tests added in `src/testInvert.test.ts` verify the behavior under both `invert: true` and `invert: 2` combined with `skipInternal: true`.
